gloss: to defect; to turn against; to become estranged
notes:
Describes the process of supporters, allies, or members breaking away from a group or leader. Implies that loyalty or support existed before and has been withdrawn. Very common in political and organizational contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {支持者|しじしゃ}の{離反|りはん}: defection of supporters
- {離反|りはん}を{招|まね}く: to invite/cause defection
- ～から{離反|りはん}する: to turn against ~, to break away from ~
- {離反|りはん}{行為|こうい}: act of defection
- {民心|みんしん}の{離反|りはん}: alienation of the public

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {裏切|うらぎ}る: to betray — stronger; implies treachery and breaking trust
- {脱退|だったい}する: to withdraw, to quit — more neutral; formally leaving an organization
- {反旗|はんき}を{翻|ひるがえ}す: to raise the flag of revolt — a more dramatic expression for rebelling
- {疎遠|そえん}になる: to become estranged — gradual drifting apart without active rebellion

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {離|り} (separate, leave) + {反|はん} (oppose, rebel).

definitions.gloss: to defect; to turn against; to become estranged
definitions.explanation: to break away from a group, leader, or cause one previously supported; to become disloyal or estranged

examples.japanese: {支持者|しじしゃ}が{離反|りはん}した。
{党内|とうない}から{離反|りはん}する{議員|ぎいん}が{相次|あいつ}いだ。
examples.english: Lawmakers who defected from within the party came one after another.

examples.japanese: {国民|こくみん}の{離反|りはん}を{招|まね}いた{政策|せいさく}は{見直|みなお}すべきだ。
examples.english: Policies that caused public alienation should be reconsidered.

examples.japanese: {度重|たびかさ}なるスキャンダルにより、{多|おお}くのファンがあのアイドルから{離反|りはん}してしまった。
examples.english: Due to repeated scandals, many fans turned against that idol.
